Italy approves anti-semitism law despite concerns over freedom of expression
results.content: Italy's ​parliament on Tuesday approved a new bill aimed at combating anti-semitism – which lists some forms of criticism of ⁠Israel as examples of anti-semitic conduct – despite concerns that it could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights. The law will not impose financial ⁠penalties or criminal sanctions for offenders.

results.title: 2027 AFCON qualifiers: Senegal and 5 other nations secure spot
results.content: The first teams to qualify for the 2027 AFCON have been decided. Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco are among them.

results.title: Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
results.content: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska on Tuesday, completing a political comeback in a state that US President Donald Trump has repeatedly won by wide margins. Her victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their biggest net gain in Senate seats since 1958.

results.title: Xi Jinping calls for global cooperation on AI and free trade at APEC summit
results.content: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.

results.title: 'Taylor Swift of games': Grand Theft Auto is back after 13-year wait
results.content: "Grand Theft Auto" will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles on Thursday after 13 years of waiting, two delays and several leaks. The global gaming phenomenon – dubbed the "Taylor Swift of games" – is the most expensive video game ever developed, and it is on track to break sales records.

results.title: Haitians rally behind Bukele as Salvadoran troops battle gangs
results.content: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to urge El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting gangs, as his troops bolster security forces in the Caribbean nation. But experts warn that growing public support could turn to anger without a long-term plan to tackle violence and strengthen Haiti's police.

results.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of historic three-way summit with Putin, Xi
results.content: US President Donald Trump arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of a high-stakes trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and China's leader Xi Pinging on Thursday. The meeting has sparked fears that the three men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.

results.title: Middle East live: Tehran warns of 'more devastating' response to attacks on Iran
results.content: Iran's army chief Amir Hatami said on Wednesday that his country will retaliate in a “more devastating” manner if the United States and its allies launch new attacks on its territory. Earlier that day, Iran's official IRNA news agency reported that Washington had hit Qeshm Island without causing serious damage, while Kuwait and Bahrain said that they intercepted hostile strikes. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

results.title: Nvidia board rules that co-founder Jensen Huang will not return as CEO
results.content: Nvidia's board chairman ruled out bringing back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Tuesday, as the chipmaker forecast stronger-than-expected quarterly sales but faced growing questions over its leadership, national security exposure and long-term strategy following his abrupt departure.

results.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
results.content: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.

results.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
results.content: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.

results.title: 🔴Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new Knesset speaker
Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
results.content: The Israeli parliament on Tuesday elected as new speaker an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matan Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu.

results.title: AI imagery complicates Nigeria's election preparations
results.content: In tonight's edition: Concerns emerge that artificial intelligence has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Also, Nigeria's mining marshal heads underground to unearth some of the people and organisations behind the vast illegal mining industries. Plus a groundbreaking archaeological discovery in northern Sudan could be the ancient site of the largest church ever built in one of medieval Nubia's most important Christian sites.

results.title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
results.content: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

results.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be honoured to return to Nvidia as CEO
results.content: Jensen Huang makes his first public statement since resigning from Nvidia, saying he'd be honoured to return to his job amid support from the tech world. It comes ahead of a much anticipated earnings call this Tuesday, with analysts expecting the group to report a 90% jump in revenue to about $109 billion.

results.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang: Targeted by the AI misinformation he helped create
results.content: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has become the target of a wave of AI-generated misinformation, in a striking twist for one of the men behind the AI revolution. From a fake audio recording supposedly featuring his wife to fabricated LinkedIn profiles, false claims linking him to the Chinese Communist Party and viral AI memes, Vedika Bahl examines how deepfakes and misinformation are turning against the former tech boss in Truth or Fake.

results.title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
results.content: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".

results.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
results.content: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.

results.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
results.content: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.

results.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
results.content: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.
